page.layout: One column of running text; marginal notes in the right margin beside the lines "Item Sex" and "reuocādo perferri"; catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: propter regulā, Legitimè res uendita & tradita emptoris esto. Quæsitum est enim, legitimé ne uendita res esset: quod negatur. Ex quo intelligi debet, non contractum uenditionis, sed Greek [illegible, ~4 letters]συναλλαγμα [?], id est, permutationem & æqualitatem rei cum precio dominium trâsferre. Item Sexaliud [illegible, ~4 letters]tianæ caufæ status definitionis est. Lex est: Qui uim publicè fecerit, poenas luito. P. Sextius, ut lex de Cicerone reuocādo perferri posset, nec ui à Clodianis impediretur, præsidium armatorum hominum habuit: cumque iis etiā pugnauit. Accusatur à M.[illegible, ~5 letters] Al-

page.notes: The Greek word after "sed" is printed in a small, blurred face; the reading συναλλαγμα is a guess and is marked [?]. The marginal marks at "Item Sex" and at "reuocādo" are in a non-Latin script and could not be read letter by letter. The word "Sextianæ" is split by the marginal mark. The catchword "Al-" is the start of the next page. Printing forms "est", "sed" and "poffet" were written with a plain s.
